summary: SIEM feed c012_broker_nic is severely degraded by sustained oversubscription: VF-1 port 5 (1 Gbps to SIEM) is at 100% average load and dropping ~50.7% of packets, plus SIEM eth1 dropping another ~4.9% on ingress. SIEM is missing more than half of events.

findings.root_cause: Egress port VF-1 port 5 is oversubscribed - average load at line-rate (100% of 1 Gbps) with bursts higher, causing broker output tail drops (11,003,520 packets, 50.67% lost). Downstream SIEM eth1 also cannot keep up and discards 525,000 received packets (4.90% lost), indicating both broker egress and tool ingress are overrun.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM misses ~50% of forwarded traffic plus additional ~5% at its own NIC. Detection coverage is halved, correlation and alerting are incomplete, and burst traffic/incidents are likely invisible.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM needs_full_payload=false and needs_both_directions=false, so volume can be safely reduced at the packet broker to fit the 1 Gbps tool port. Filtering to security-relevant flows/protocols or sampling will eliminate the 50% broker drops. If full traffic is required, use load_balance across multiple SIEM receivers or upgrade to 10 Gbps (tool_capacity).
